protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; one owner-recording entry for DR-002 under adopted D-054 / D-057; own cycle, not D-059
summary: The subject held frozen and every attack fails. My finding from the combined draft is repaired at the root: D-057's pin list is now satisfied in full, with the disposition and both verdicts given as complete paths beside their sha256s and 'ACCEPT 0/0' stated for each, which also evidences D-057's dual-ACCEPT-at-0-blockers precondition rather than leaving it to be discovered. The Route A remainder is not merely present but provably complete — I compared it against the disposition's own whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA field programmatically and the two lists are an exact four-item match. The turn-1 combined subject is pinned at 81b67b5b, which is the digest I actually reviewed, and my finding is attributed with the right id and severity. All four artifact digests and all four commits verify. One note: this is the second frozen D-058 draft dispatched to me in the same turn, and only one can be adopted.

notesRecorded.location: cycle bookkeeping, not the entry's content
notesRecorded.observation: Two distinct frozen D-058 drafts were dispatched to me in this same turn, each under its own review prompt, and I have now consented to both. This one is coordinator-decisions.D-058.draft.md at 79f2e4ed01159bea8e472b93e571f30b8f813fb4946bd3b7ddf2cc60c0020f6c under coordinator-decisions.D-058.review-prompt.md. The other is coordinator-decisions.D-058.owner.draft.md at b2b2ed0fa371d57d60e80db8749f377fdf75180bdf1dabd9a5d5023239258cda under coordinator-decisions.D-058.owner.review-prompt.md, verdict written to coordinator-decisions.D-058.owner.review-adversarial.claude2.json.
notesRecorded.whyItIsNotAFinding: Both drafts record the same decision on the same row from the same pinned disposition and verdicts, both satisfy D-057's pin list, and neither asserts anything the other contradicts. Nothing in either file is wrong, so there is nothing in these bytes to fix.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecording: They are not byte-identical and they carry different structures — this one leads with a turn-1 disposition table and a standalone Route A section, the other carries the same content inside numbered clauses. Only one should be adopted as D-058, and the adopted entry should cite the verdict written against the draft it actually adopts. Adopting one while citing the other's verdict digest would break the audit link this corpus depends on. Recorded so the choice is deliberate rather than incidental.
notesRecorded.alsoObserved: Two earlier drafts covering this same row were dispatched and objected to in this session — the D-058/D-059 combined draft at 81b67b5b, which this entry correctly supersedes and pins, and the five-entry D-059-063 draft at 5a7cc743, whose D-059 records DR-002. Neither this file nor that one states their relationship.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 79f2e4ed01159bea8e472b93e571f30b8f813fb4946bd3b7ddf2cc60c0020f6c, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest. The dispatch made motion an OBJECT condition and it does not arise.

The attack 'D-057 pin list incomplete (paths, not basenames; both verdict paths; full Route-A remainder)' fails on all three limbs, and this is the repair of the finding I raised on the combined draft. The Authority and dependency pins section gives the disposition as a full path with sha256, and each verdict as a full path with sha256 — 'docs/coop/artifacts/route-b.DR-002.preview-disposition.v2.review-independent.claude2.json' and the codex.json — with both also carrying 'ACCEPT 0/0' in the measured-inputs table. Where the combined draft had zero verdict path strings, this has them in two places.

That same repair closes the precondition gap I raised separately on the five-entry draft: D-057 requires dual independent ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers, and 'ACCEPT 0/0' is now stated for both reviewers. The Claude 2 half is exactly what I returned on that disposition.

The Route A remainder is complete, which I tested rather than read. I compared the entry's four items against the disposition's own whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA field by string equality: four items each, exact match, same order — focused independent AC-1 adjudication; repaired validator successor plus claim-register motion (AC-3); eight-bullet Phase-1A packet (AC-4 / DR-004); full V10 / G19 / publication-block (not this row's close; D-030 / D-028).

The turn-1 provenance is accurate. The combined subject is pinned at 81b67b5b41edcd0cf5f9db94d11519ad456104e20f5ae43e6444138b9522db1e, which is the digest I measured and reviewed, and my finding is attributed as 'Claude 2 SHOULD-FIX C2-D058059-01' — matching my verdict exactly, which was OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX with that single id.
All four cited artifact digests match live bytes: the D-054 user amendment, the DR-002 v2 disposition, and both v2 verdicts. COORD and file 08 also match.
All four cited commits resolve at full hash to the expected decisions: 29670ed… D-054, 33597e8… D-057, aa75926… D-047/D-048, 88764fa… D-049/D-050.

The attack 'bundled with D-059 (must be own cycle)' fails three ways: the protocol line states 'This file is one owner-recording entry and one cycle'; the header states '**Does not** owner-record DR-004 or any other row'; and clause 5 states 'Does not owner-record DR-003, DR-004, DR-005, or DR-008.' The disposition table records ADV-D058-059-T1-01 as accepted with 'This file is D-058 only.'

The attack 'discharges AC-1/AC-3/AC-4' fails. Clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-002 SATISFIED. The Route A remainder above stays owed', and that remainder names AC-1, AC-3 and AC-4 explicitly as owed. Clause 2 keeps the effect conditional and bounded: 'may discharge condition 1 for DR-002 within architecture-preview scope only.'
The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: the header refuses it, clause 3 refuses it, and the Readiness effect states 'Zero SATISFIED.'

The attacks 'file 08 edited' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail: the header refuses both, clause 3 states 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', clause 4 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6). A later cell note is a separate act', file 08 measures unchanged and git reports zero modified tracked files.

The dependency declaration D-057 requires is present in the required form: 'Dependencies: D-054, D-057, and D-047. Revocation or overturn requires this owner's supersession and reconciliation of dependent MF-6 notes.'

The rider statement is correct and reasoned rather than blank: 'Operative riders: none. D-049 recorded ACCEPT 0/0 with no rider. No ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES advisories to classify.' That is right for this row — both v2 verdicts were ACCEPT at 0 advisories, unlike DR-005 where D-039's RB-DR005-V2-A1 would have to travel.

The owner role matches file 08's DR-002 owner cell: 'Evidence authority + V1 coordinator'. Reversibility is the correct compound form and does not reach back into its authorities: 'Compound. Overturn: C-D058, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note. Does not overturn D-047, D-049, D-054, or D-057.'

Examined and declined: the entry cites the prior cycle's findings by id and severity but pins neither reviewer's verdict digest, pinning only the prior subject. This is a new cycle rather than a later turn, so the prior verdicts pertain to a superseded subject, and I confirmed the one characterization I can check — my own — is exact. I applied the same reasoning when I declined the analogous point on D-057 turn 3.

I verified the resulting bytes — own cycle, full paths, full Route A remainder — rather than the characterizations, and I note that Codex appears to have independently found the verdict-paths defect I raised, which is corroboration I cannot confirm.
The Codex verdict on the DR-002 v2 disposition. Its digest verifies but I did not open it, so the dual half of D-057's dual-ACCEPT precondition rests on this entry's recital of 'ACCEPT 0/0'.

Which of the two frozen D-058 drafts should be adopted, or how either relates to the five-entry D-059-063 draft whose D-059 records this same row. See the note; the entries do not state it and I graded only the bytes each dispatch gave me.
The merits of the DR-002 v2 disposition beyond my separate ACCEPT review of it, whose stated limits I carry forward.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The finding I raised against the combined draft is repaired in the strongest form — the disposition and both verdicts as full paths with sha256s and stated verdict classes — and that repair closes the precondition gap I raised separately on the five-entry draft. The axis I tested hardest was completeness of the Route A remainder, because 'from the pinned disposition' is a claim that can be checked: I compared it field to field and it is an exact four-item match. My one note is not about these bytes but about which of them get adopted: two frozen D-058 drafts reached me in the same turn and I have consented to both, so the adopted entry needs to cite the verdict written against the draft it actually adopts.
